draft.title: Analysing an extract
card: An extract is a short passage from the text you have studied. The question wants you to use its details as evidence, not to retell it.
Start with the details in front of you: word choices, techniques, images, and the speaker or setting. Say what each one suggests about a character, idea or value.
Then link those details to the whole text. Show how the extract repeats, develops or changes a pattern, such as a motif, a theme or a character's journey.
Keep your argument tied to the question. Use the extract as your main evidence, and bring in other parts of the text only to show the wider pattern.
draft.remember: Read closely, then widen out: the extract is evidence for an argument about the whole text.

a.q: A student's response to an extract describes each sentence in order, then stops. What is the main thing missing?
opts: A link between the extract's details and the whole text
A longer summary of what happens in the extract
A quotation from every line of the extract
A list of every technique in the whole text
a.why: An extract response should use close details to say something about the patterns and ideas of the whole text. Retelling in order, even at length, does not do this, so a longer summary is not the fix.
a.clue: The extract is a small part of something bigger.

b.q: Dev is analysing an extract in which a character looks out a window at a storm. Dev notes the harsh verbs describing the storm. Which next step best fits the advice for analysing an extract?
opts: Show how the storm imagery ties to a pattern in the text
Describe the same storm scene again in simpler words
Move on to a different scene and drop the extract
Compare the extract with another text Dev has studied
b.why: After noting details, the next step is to connect them to a wider pattern or idea in the studied text. Retelling adds no argument. Comparing with another text drifts from the question about this extract and its own text.
b.clue: After the details, widen out to the whole text.

a.best: A link between the extract's details and the whole text

b.best: Show how the storm imagery ties to a pattern in the text
